text:
Ajay Gupta: Quick onboarding question — customer needs an egress allowlist for our hosted inference endpoints. They can't run a proxy in their env. What is the minimal set of things we should give them (IPs / hostnames / ports)?

Devon Lee: Short answer: give them region-scoped static egress IP blocks + hostnames for SNI as fallback. Also ask if they do TLS MITM (corp TLS inspection) — that breaks cert pinning.

Devon Lee: Recommended checklist for customers:
• Allow outbound TCP 443 to our regional NAT pools (we provide CIDRs).
• Allow DNS to resolve our hostnames (UDP/TCP 53) or proxy needs DNS passthrough.
• Prefer domain/SNI allowlist: `*.redwood-inference.com` and `api.redwood.red` (region specific).
• If they use a proxy, ensure CONNECT to port 443 is allowed and we support `Proxy-Authorization` header if auth is required.

Maria Chen: One gotcha: ephemeral port churn + return path. Some corporate firewalls block ephemeral source ports. Tell them to allow ephemeral high ports (1024-65535) for return traffic or at least 32768-61000 depending on their stack.

Ajay Gupta: Do we have a canonical example firewall rule we can paste into the onboarding ticket?

Devon Lee: Yep — example (simple):
```
# Allow outbound to Redwood (example CIDRs, replace with region-specific blocks we provide)
ALLOW TCP 443 TO 34.210.32.0/24
ALLOW TCP 443 TO 34.210.33.0/24
# DNS for resolution
ALLOW UDP/TCP 53 TO ANY
# Ephemeral return ports (if stateful, might not be needed)
ALLOW TCP/UDP 32768-61000 FROM ANY
```
Note: we don't publish global single-IP; we give per-customer region pools.

Lina (support): Customer asked about IP rotation — how often do the NAT IPs change? They want SLA that IPs won't change mid-month.

Devon Lee: We try to avoid rotations but we do maintenance and capacity moves. For customers that need static stable IPs without rotation, recommend Dedicated or Private deployments (reserved egress NAT). For Hosted customers we can offer a stable small pool for an additional commitment (add to the onboarding ticket and escalate to sales/infra).

Maria Chen: Operational note — observability: if they allow only our IPs, we still need them to whitelist DNS to avoid failures when we rotate CNAMEs. Also we should add an alert to our ops when a customer reports blocked traffic: check for TLS handshake failures and increased 403/523 patterns.

Ajay Gupta: Got it. Anything about headers or SNI?

Devon Lee: If they insist on IP-only (no domain), warn them about IP drift and certificate mismatch for SNI-based routing. If they can allow by SNI, it's much simpler: they only allow outbound TCP/443 and allow SNI hostname `*.redwood-inference.com` at their edge firewall. We also send a weekly "egress IP list" to customers who opt-in to notify about planned changes.

Maria Chen: Also include this question in the checklist: "Are you doing TLS MITM / corporate proxy interception?" If yes, we require customer to allow `CONNECT` to our hostnames and provide proxy credentials or use a Private deployment.

infra-bot: Heads up — scheduled egress pool maintenance on 2025-07-12 02:00 UTC; small set of hosted IPs may be moved across AZs, customers will be notified who opted into egress alerts.

Lina (support): Action items: 1) Add example CIDRs + domain allowlist to onboarding ticket. 2) Flag customers that require IP-immutability and route to sales/infra plan. 3) Add ephemeral-port note to KB. I'll create the ticket.

Ajay Gupta: Awesome — please paste the final snippet into the onboarding template and include the opt-in checkbox for egress-change notifications. Thanks :thumbsup:
